source.title: AlphaAlign: Incentivizing Safety Alignment with Extremely Simplified Reinforcement Learning
source.authors: Yi Zhang; An Zhang; XiuYu Zhang; Leheng Sheng; Yuxin Chen; Zhen-Kai Liang; Xiang Wang

record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates jailbreak attack success and uses a different, heuristic token-position metric to assess whether its alignment method produces deeper safety behavior.
record.gate_note: The study reports attack success rates after AlphaAlign training and CKAS curves for selected keywords. It does not measure aligned-versus-base per-token KL, fine-tuning on a few harmful or benign examples, or localized safety parameters. CKAS is a keyword-propensity metric, not a direct measurement of safety behavior at each response position.
record.test_reason: AlphaAlign is an RL safety method the authors present as a fix for shallow alignment (RQ4). They report jailbreak ASR before and after training on three instruct models, so the results bear on V7 by a different method. The untrained instruct baselines under GCG (suffix) and PAIR (a 'begin with Sure, here is' instruction) bear weakly on V4. There is no per-token KL, no prefilling attack, no fine-tuning attack and no parameter localization.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that verifiable-reward RL with a helpfulness reward improves refusal and jailbreak robustness and reduces over-refusal while largely keeping utility. They read higher CKAS for safety words as evidence of deeper alignment. Utility is not uniformly kept: Llama3.2-3B loses 8.3 points on GSM8K.
record.recipe_differences: This is a new PPO-based RL safety-alignment method with verifiable refusal and format rewards plus a normalized helpfulness reward; it is not a reproduction of the cited fine-tuning or few-tokens-depth methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by model and benchmark. The paper evaluates different backbone models and attack benchmarks; CKAS is shown for Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct under PAIR attacks.

fits_no_version.finding: CKAS on Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct under PAIR: AlphaAlign raises the score for safety words ('illegal', 'harm') and lowers it for 'here' in early response positions (Fig. 5, figure only).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reasoning-based RL alignment shifts early-token keyword propensity toward safety terms and away from compliant openings.

record.problems: The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for the listed results. CKAS is explicitly a heuristic keyword-probability measure, not a direct measure of safety behavior across response positions. The authors also note that larger-model performance was not investigated.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 CoCoNot over-refusal scores were omitted because they measure benign-prompt over-refusal rather than harmful compliance or the listed attack/deepening outcomes. Table 3 utility scores were omitted because they do not measure the claim versions. Other baseline methods in Tables 2–3 were not separately rowed; the rows retain AlphaAlign outcomes against the unaligned model baseline.

untested.parts: No harmful fine-tuning attack on any model.
No prefilling of a compliant start and no decoding-parameter attacks. Only GCG suffixes and PAIR prompt-instructed openings are evaluated.
No test of what data or objective produces shallowness.

Whether AlphaAlign holds up against prefilling attacks or subsequent fine-tuning attacks. Whether safety is actually present at later response positions (no positional refusal or KL measure). Models larger than 7B.

missing.what: Untrained instruct-model ASR under GCG and PAIR as standalone attack-success rows: Qwen2.5-3B GCG 49.04/PAIR 67.69; Llama3.2-3B GCG 13.24/PAIR 10.76; Qwen2.5-7B GCG 10.96/PAIR 44.42.
Direct Refusal (shallow SFT on same data) jailbreak ASR as the comparison for depth-specific gains, e.g. Qwen2.5-3B PAIR 11.54, GCG 5.77; Qwen2.5-7B PAIR 0.19, GCG 0.57.
AlphaAlign-Zero on base Qwen2.5-3B: jailbreak ASR vs Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, and training dynamics.
Utility costs of AlphaAlign (e.g. Llama3.2-3B GSM8K -8.3, MMLU -2.1).

record.verdict_notes: The record misplaced the Qwen2.5-3B WildGuardTest and JailbreakTrigger values (correct: 6.38 and 3.75). The reader's V4 'supports' label rested on residual ASR after AlphaAlign, which is not what V4 claims; it is replaced with labels based on the untrained baselines. The depth claim rests on a keyword heuristic, not on prefilling or fine-tuning attacks. No uncertainty estimates are given. The models are 3B-7B only.

versions.untested_parts: The study trains for safety with RL; it does not test whether fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred harmful examples removes safety.
The benign data is part of a safety-alignment RL procedure, not a test of whether ordinary or carefully chosen benign fine-tuning data raises harmful compliance.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL divergence is measured.
PAIR and GCG attacks are evaluated, but the study does not isolate the effect of a compliant prefilled opening or test decoding changes.
No weight or rank localization analysis is reported.
The study does not test whether a particular data property or training objective causes safety to be shallow.

The study reports a keyword-based proxy and benchmark outcomes, not whether actual safety behavior is distributed across response positions or whether the effect persists beyond the reported evaluations.

relationships.condition: Jailbreak benchmarks (WildGuardTest, JailbreakTrigger, PAIR, GCG) on Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Llama3.2-3B-Instruct
relationships.reason: AlphaAlign cuts jailbreak ASR sharply (e.g. PAIR 67.69 to 4.61, GCG 49.04 to 0.77) and beats Direct Refusal SFT on most of these (r3-r6, r9-r12).
relationships.display_finding: AlphaAlign cut attack success sharply, for example PAIR from 67.69 to 4.61 and GCG from 49.04 to 0.77, and beat direct-refusal SFT on most of these benchmarks.

relation.reason: Its own jailbreak measurements and alignment-depth analysis bear on V4 and V7.

tranche.reason: The study tests a proposed remedy for shallow alignment using RL, jailbreak ASR, and a keyword-based depth proxy rather than reproducing the original method.

source_check.notes: CKAS measures keyword adoption along greedy continuations, not aligned-versus-base per-token KL or a causal effect of depth. Table 3 also reports an 8.3-point GSM8K decline for Llama3.2-3B-Instruct.

statements.correction: Table 2: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct Direct Refusal and AlphaAlign both obtain PAIR ASR 0.19% and JailbreakTrigger ASR 0.25%. Appendix C.1: AlphaAlign uses sampled harmful and Dolly data; other baselines use the full Circuit Breaker dataset, equally many augmented harmful examples, and complete Dolly and XSTest datasets. Alignment depth is not independently manipulated.
statements.problem: The numerical ties and caution about causal attribution are correct, but the condition's description of a matched comparator overstates the controls: training data and procedures differ. CLS claims concern another study and are outside this check.
